items.title: Shri Chitrapur Math, Shirali
items.hook: The spiritual home of the Chitrapur Saraswat community.
paras: The Shri Chitrapur Math is the math of the Chitrapur Saraswat Brahmin community. Its headquarters is at Shirali, in Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka.

The community traces its roots to the Saraswat Brahmins who settled along the Kanara coast. The math has guided the community's religious and cultural life for generations, and runs schools, hostels and charitable work alongside its spiritual role.
Its temples and shrines are cared for by the math, and the community gathers at Shirali through the year.
items.wow: The community's members are spread across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Goa and overseas, but Shirali remains the centre.

items.title: Shrimad Partagali Jeevottam Math
items.hook: The Gaud Saraswat math in Goa.
paras: The Shrimad Partagali Jeevottam Math stands at Partagali in Canacona, south Goa, and is one of the principal maths of the Gaud Saraswat Brahmin community.
It is named after Shrimad Jeevottam Teerth, and its deity is Shri Ramnath. The math has a long tradition of scholarship and of looking after temples in the region.
Its annual festivals draw GSB families from Goa, Karnataka, Maharashtra and beyond.
items.wow: The Gaud Saraswat community is often called the GSB, and its maths in Goa and at Kashi are both central to its identity.

items.title: Shri Kashi Math Samsthan
items.hook: A Konkani community's math, far away in Varanasi.
paras: The Shri Kashi Math Samsthan is a math of the Gaud Saraswat Brahmin community with its headquarters at Varanasi (Kashi).
It traces its line of spiritual heads back centuries, and its branches and followers are spread through coastal Karnataka, Goa, Kerala and Maharashtra.
The math runs temples, schools and charitable institutions, and its swamijis travel to the community's centres through the year.
items.wow: For a coastal community, having its math in Kashi is a reminder of how far Saraswat families travelled for scholarship.

items.title: Shri Shantadurga Temple, Kavlem
items.hook: The goddess who is said to have settled a quarrel.
paras: The Shri Shantadurga temple at Kavlem in Ponda, Goa, is one of the most visited temples of the Gaud Saraswat community.
The name Shantadurga means the goddess of peace. Tradition says she mediated between Shiva and Vishnu, and the temple's annual jatra is a major event in Goa.
The present temple was built in the 18th century, after the original shrine was moved from its older site.
items.wow: Several Goan temples, including this one, were relocated inland in the 16th century to keep them safe.

items.title: Shri Mangesh Temple, Priol
items.hook: A Shiva temple that belongs to the community.
paras: The Shri Mangesh temple at Priol (Mangeshi) in Ponda, Goa, is dedicated to Shiva and is closely tied to the Gaud Saraswat Brahmin community.
The temple is known for its deepstambha, its tank and its distinctive Goan architecture, and its annual festivals draw large crowds.
Like Shantadurga, the temple was moved to its present site in the 16th century.
items.wow: The Mangesh temple's architecture mixes Goan and Konkani styles, and it is one of the best-known temples in Goa.

items.title: Konkani across four states
paras: Konkani is spoken along the western coast, from Maharashtra through Goa and coastal Karnataka to northern Kerala.
It is the official language of Goa and is written in Devanagari, though Roman script is also widely used by communities in Mangalore and Kochi.
Konkani-speaking communities settled in Kanhangad in Kerala and in Kochi over centuries, and their temples and maths are still active today.
items.wow: Konkani was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution in 1992.

items.title: The Saraswat thread
items.hook: Chitrapur and Gaud Saraswat are not the same community.
paras: The Konkani Saraswat world has two large branches: the Gaud Saraswat Brahmins and the Chitrapur Saraswats.
The Gaud Saraswats are spread across Goa, coastal Karnataka and Kerala, and follow the Partagali and Kashi maths.
The Chitrapur Saraswats are a smaller community centred on Shirali in Karnataka, with their own math and their own traditions.
items.wow: Both branches share the Konkani language and a coastal heritage, but their maths and customs are distinct.
